narrative: Material PL1__M115A2E8 exhibits erratic, right-skewed daily demand (CV=0.53) with a statistically significant upward trend over the observation window, and a moderate lead time CV of 0.38, creating meaningful combined demand-lead time uncertainty. The current SAP safety stock of 85 units is critically insufficient — it covers only ~0.23 days of mean demand against a lead time exceeding 2.7 days. A (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 820 units and an EOQ-derived order quantity of 602 units achieves the 95% service level target while reducing annual total inventory cost by approximately 39.8% through order consolidation.
warnings: SAP safety stock (85) is far below the analytically derived safety stock (820); stockout risk under current policy is high.
Upward demand trend detected — safety stock and reorder point should be reviewed quarterly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (95.5% non-zero working days) with erratic but non-intermittent behaviour; a continuous-review reorder-point policy with EOQ-sized orders efficiently balances holding and ordering costs under moderate lead time variability without requiring complex stochastic optimization.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The jump from 85 to 820 safety stock units increases average on-hand inventory materially, raising annual holding cost; however this is necessary to meet the 95% service level — operating at the SAP level exposes the business to frequent stockouts given sigma_ltd of ~498 units.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — safety_stock + order_quantity (1422) is well within max_storage_units (2234.6); MOQ constraint (81) is satisfied by the recommended order quantity of 602.
